notes:
Passed on the fake backend by python3 -m mhs.driver check (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). Model-authored and unreviewed; no hardware backend and no hardware run was made. Robot SF was not importable where the gate ran, so the fake backend is the package's own kinematic stand-in (fake.py) and was never compared with the upstream environment. The fake reduces the fused observation: drive_state is 4 values (two robot speeds and a target vector) and rays is 8 constant ranges, while the real environment returns a Dict with 272 LiDAR rays by default (robot_sf/sensor/range_sensor.py:148) and a stacked target vector; the real array size is named here and in the fidelity gaps. Social-force pedestrians, obstacles, collisions, the route-completion reward and route/collision terminal conditions are not modelled; only the default simulated time limit (200.0 s at 0.1 s per step) terminates an episode. The fake uses a simple unicycle Euler pose update instead of wheel-speed odometry. Robot SF registers its environments in its own registry (env id robot), not with gymnasium, so no sim backend (gymnasium.make) is provided and none was run. Expected warnings: G6.NO_NATIVE_CALL for cap.world.seed.v1 (it only sets the pending seed, no native call) and four G8.NO_UNIT for bridge-derived inputs (ticks, both seed inputs and action.values); there were no G4.REF_VALUE or G4.REF_BINARY warnings. Only catalogue classes are used, so there are no catalogue requests. gate.digest is the digest the check printed; check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run and is not part of the package.
